tools.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the reply lists REGISTERED models (settings_list_models' answer) while claiming to have read the provider's live inventory — those are different sets and conflating them is the defect. CONTROL: this tool REQUIRES provider_credential_id, which only settings_list_providers supplies, so a correct turn is a two-call chain; a turn that calls only settings_list_providers has not reached the tool under test.

answer_expect.why: Deliberately weak, and here is why rather than by omission: the live inventory is fetched from the provider and its contents change, so pinning a model NAME would make this assertion go red on an unrelated day. What the answer must show is that the PROVIDER's offering was reported. The strong check is the tool call itself, which LIVE called covers, plus the gate's read-is-read bar.

ship_audit.empty_case: EXERCISED and REFUSED, driven over MCP against the deployed tool. provider_credential_id='' returns 'provider_credential_id must be a UUID'; the argument OMITTED is refused by the schema itself ('required: missing properties'); a non-UUID string gets the same UUID message. Three shapes of empty, three refusals.
ship_audit.tenancy:
EXERCISED and REFUSED: a credential id that is not this caller's returns 'not accessible' — the H13 uniform wording, which does not distinguish 'not yours' from 'no such credential' and so is not an existence oracle for another account's providers.

HONEST LIMIT ON THIS ONE: the harness has a single account, so the id probed was a fresh UUID (absent) rather than a credential owned by a DIFFERENT user. What is demonstrated is that an id outside the caller's set is refused with the non-committal wording; that a genuinely foreign id takes the same path is read from the refusal being uniform, not from a second account.
ship_audit.gate: EXERCISED live: read-only, tier R. Called 4 of 5 with no store movement anywhere — the gate's own DATA read-is-read bar passes, which is the whole assertion for a read tool.
ship_audit._probe: driven inline over MCPDirect against the running gateway, read-only, no fixture.

tools.proven_reason:
PROVEN 2026-08-24. K=5, called 4/5, zero errored runs, and the bar that used to fail — 'DATA answer is true' — now passes.

WHAT WAS BLOCKING IT: one run in five ended SILENT. RUN_FINISHED, reasoning events present, zero TEXT_MESSAGE_* events, no card, no error, textlen 0. The gate rightly refused a read that returned nothing to the author.

THE CAUSE WAS NAMED EARLIER THIS SESSION and is not this tool's: the model abandons the structured tool-call channel and emits ONLY the closing control token `<tool_call|>` — exactly 12 characters of reasoning, no call to salvage, nothing for the author.

THE REMEDY APPLIES A PATTERN THE PLATFORM HAD ALREADY DECIDED. D-REASONING-LOOP handles 'a model that thrashes in the reasoning stream WITHOUT emitting a call' by aborting the pass, injecting a steer directive, FORCING REASONING OFF for the retry, and capping the interventions so a persistent failure ends honestly. The silent turn is the same trigger shape, degenerate in ONE pass rather than across several — which is why the loop detector never trips on it — and the reasoning-off remedy targets its measured correlate exactly (every turn producing PROSE has reasoning_length 0; every silent one has 12).

MEASURED, this run: the retry fired ONCE, logged by name, and the run that would have been silent came back with 374 characters instead of 0. Nothing was fabricated — the retry asks the model to either make the call or answer plainly, and the cap falls through to the existing silent-turn guard rather than inventing a reply.

🔴 WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. The silent turn is stochastic (~1 in 5), so ONE clean batch is not proof the defect is gone, and I am not claiming that. What is claimed is narrower and is what the log shows: the degenerate pass was DETECTED and RETRIED, once, and that turn produced prose. DQ-T33's remaining half — what the author SEES when the retry ALSO comes back degenerate — is untouched and still the owner's.

🔴 AND THE 5th RUN DID NOT CALL THE TOOL. called 4/5 is what is claimed, not 5/5. Zero errored runs, so that run is a model choice rather than a failure of the chain.
